match.reason: Neither bank point teaches recording GST collected and paid through a GST Clearing account; the maths point covers calculating GST and the inventory point covers cost price, so both are related but different ideas.

draft.title: Recording GST
card: GST is a 10% tax added to most goods and services in Australia. A business collects it from customers and pays it on its own purchases.
GST charged on sales. It is owed to the tax office, so it is recorded as a credit in the GST Clearing account.
GST paid on purchases. The business can claim it back, so it is recorded as a debit in the GST Clearing account.

If the credits (GST collected) are larger than the debits (GST paid), the account has a credit balance. The business owes that amount to the tax office. If the debits are larger, the tax office owes the business a refund.
draft.remember: GST Clearing: credit for GST collected, debit for GST paid. The balance shows who owes whom.

a.q: Priya's Cycles sells a bike for $1100 including $100 GST. How is the $100 GST recorded in the GST Clearing account?
opts: Credit, because it is owed to the tax office
Debit, because it is owed to the tax office
Credit, because it can be claimed back
Debit, because it can be claimed back
a.why: The $100 was collected from the customer on a sale, and the business must pass it on to the tax office. Money owed is recorded as a credit. A debit is for GST paid on purchases, which can be claimed back.
a.clue: Was the GST charged on a sale or paid on a purchase?

b.q: In one quarter, Tom's Timber has $6000 in GST collected and $7500 in GST paid. What does the GST Clearing account show?
opts: A debit balance of $1500, so a refund is due to Tom
A credit balance of $1500, so Tom owes the tax office
A debit balance of $6000, so a refund is due to Tom
A credit balance of $7500, so Tom owes the tax office
b.why: GST paid ($7500) is debited and GST collected ($6000) is credited. The debits are larger by $1500, so the account has a debit balance and the tax office owes Tom a refund. A credit balance would mean Tom had collected more than he paid.
b.clue: Subtract the smaller total from the larger, then see which side is larger.

a.best: Credit, because it is owed to the tax office

b.best: A debit balance of $1500, so a refund is due to Tom
